Community FAQ.What is Sonic Labs?: Sonic Labs is an EVM-compatible Layer-1 blockchain (rebranded from Fantom) that leverages a DAG-based aBFT consensus for ultra-fast finality and high throughput.
Community FAQ.How to stake S tokens?: To stake S tokens, you can use the official Sonic Labs staking portal at https://staking.sonic.io or through compatible wallets like MetaMask by connecting to the Sonic network.
Community FAQ.What's the minimum stake amount?: The minimum stake amount is 1 S token, making it accessible to users with small holdings.
Community FAQ.When will the next airdrop happen?: The next airdrop is scheduled for Q3 2025, targeting early users accumulating Sonic Points.
Community FAQ.How can I earn more Sonic Points?: To earn more Sonic Points, engage with the community on social media, participate in events, or complete special tasks available in the ecosystem.
Community FAQ.What is the Sonic Labs consensus mechani: Sonic Labs uses a DAG-based asynchronous Byzantine Fault Tolerant (aBFT) consensus that achieves finality in approximately 1 second, ensuring both speed and security.
Community FAQ.What is the purpose of the Sonic token (: The Sonic token (S) is the native utility token of Sonic Labs, used for staking, transaction fees, governance, and interacting with decentralized applications (dApps) within the Sonic ecosystem.
Community FAQ.How does the Sonic Labs ecosystem benefi: Sonic Labs offers low transaction fees, fast finality, and a robust SDK, providing developers with a high-performance blockchain environment for building decentralized applications.
Community FAQ.Can I use MetaMask with Sonic Labs?: Yes, you can connect your MetaMask wallet to the Sonic Labs network by adding the custom RPC for Sonic in MetaMask's network settings.
Community FAQ.What is the fee structure on Sonic Labs?: Sonic Labs uses a Fee Monetization (FeeM) model where developers can receive up to 90% of the gas fees from transactions in their dApps, making it highly developer-friendly.
Community FAQ.How do I join the Sonic Labs community?: You can join the Sonic Labs community by following them on social media, joining their Telegram or Discord groups, and participating in events or discussions about the ecosystem.
Community FAQ.How is Sonic Labs different from other b: Sonic Labs offers higher throughput (10,000 TPS under regular use) and lower latency compared to most Layer-1 blockchains, achieved through its unique aBFT consensus and DAG architecture.
Community FAQ.Are there any partnerships with Sonic La: Yes, Sonic Labs has established partnerships with several DeFi platforms like Aave, Silo Finance, and Beefy Finance, and infrastructure providers like Chainlink and Alchemy.
Community FAQ.What are Sonic Points, and how do they w: Sonic Points are loyalty points earned through network participation and interactions within the Sonic ecosystem. These points can be used for rewards, airdrops, or special community incentives.
Community FAQ.How do I get involved in the Sonic Labs: To get involved, users must hold a certain amount of S tokens and meet activity requirements set by Sonic Labs. Airdrop announcements will provide specific details on eligibility.
Community FAQ.What are the key features of Sonic Labs?: Key features include high throughput, ultra-fast finality, low fees, decentralized governance, and the unique Fee Monetization (FeeM) model for developers.
Community FAQ.Can Sonic Labs support NFTs?: Yes, Sonic Labs supports NFTs through its dApp ecosystem, enabling the creation and trade of NFTs with low fees and fast transaction speeds.
Community FAQ.What are the security measures in place: Sonic Labs implements robust security protocols through its aBFT consensus, cryptographic techniques, and partnerships with security providers like Arkham.
Community FAQ.What is the roadmap for Sonic Labs?: The roadmap includes expanding the ecosystem with more dApps, further decentralization, integration of AI-driven tools, and reaching milestones in user adoption and market cap.
Community FAQ.Is Sonic Labs available on mobile?: Yes, Sonic Labs' ecosystem is accessible through mobile wallets like MetaMask and applications integrated with the network. There are plans for a mobile app in the future.

Technical Documentation.Consensus Mechanism: Sonic Labs uses a DAG-based asynchronous Byzantine Fault Tolerant (aBFT) consensus that achieves finality in approximately 1 second.
Technical Documentation.Transaction Throughput: Sonic averages 10,000 TPS in regular operation, with peak tests reaching up to 400,000 TPS under optimal conditions.
Technical Documentation.Fee Structure: Sonic's Fee Monetization (FeeM) model allows developers to receive up to 90% of gas fees from transactions in their dApps.
Technical Documentation.Smart Contract Capabilities: Sonic Labs supports full Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) compatibility, enabling developers to deploy existing Ethereum-based smart contracts with minimal changes. The platform also provides additional tools for more complex contract logic, including built-in support for token standards (ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155) and an enhanced oracle service for secure, real-time data feeds. With the ability to execute contracts quickly and at scale, Sonic Labs is optimized for decentralized finance (DeFi), gaming, and enterprise solutions.
Technical Documentation.Security and Decentralization: Security on Sonic Labs is assured through its innovative aBFT consensus mechanism, which guarantees the network's resilience against Byzantine faults and malicious attacks. With a decentralized set of validators across multiple geographic regions, the network ensures high availability and fault tolerance. Moreover, Sonic Labs undergoes continuous security audits and collaborates with leading cybersecurity firms to ensure that the ecosystem remains safe from vulnerabilities and exploits.
Technical Documentation.Scalability: One of Sonic Labs' defining features is its ability to scale without sacrificing performance. The DAG-based architecture allows the network to process thousands of transactions in parallel, reducing bottlenecks often experienced in traditional blockchain networks. As demand grows, the system automatically adjusts by adding more nodes and validators to maintain optimal performance, making Sonic Labs a future-proof solution for a wide range of use cases, from DeFi to enterprise-level applications.

Sonic Labs Ecosystem: Latest Platforms,.Prominent DeFi Projects on Sonic Labs:
• SpookySwap (DEX): Originally Fantom’s flagship DEX, SpookySwap remains a leading decentralized exchange on Sonic. It uses an AMM model for token swaps, liquidity provision, and yield farming. Notably, SpookySwap supports features like limit orders and cross-chain bridges to Ethereum and BSC. Its native governance token BOO has migrated 1:1 from Fantom to Sonic.

• Beethoven X (AMM platform): An advanced Balancer V2 fork on Sonic, offering innovative DeFi services. Beethoven X provides weighted index pools, stable swap pools, and customizable liquidity pools (up to 8 assets) for diversified yield strategies. It serves as a decentralized investment suite on Sonic, allowing users to trade and invest with low fees and high flexibility.

• Tomb Finance (Algorithmic Stablecoin): A DeFi protocol known for its algorithmic token TOMB, designed to be pegged to Sonic’s native token S. Tomb Finance uses supply expansion and contraction mechanisms to maintain the peg, offering yield farming and bonding opportunities. This project, carried over from Fantom, continues to bolster liquidity for S by incentivizing users to farm and stake TOMB, SEN (shares), etc.

• Shadow (High-Speed DEX): A newer entrant on Sonic, Shadow is a decentralized exchange built to leverage Sonic’s ultra-fast finality. It provides near-instant swaps with minimal slippage, aligning with Sonic’s 1-second block times. Shadow also utilizes Sonic’s fee monetization (FeeM) program, refunding up to 90% of gas fees to users, which enhances the high-frequency trading experience.

• HeyAnon (AI DeFi Assistant): HeyAnon is an AI-powered DeFi platform on Sonic that simplifies user interactions with decentralized finance. It combines a conversational AI interface with real-time blockchain data to help users track investments, execute complex DeFi transactions, and analyze trends across platforms.

• Lending Protocols: Sonic is attracting lending and borrowing applications. Native Fantom platforms like Scream are expected to migrate, and even Aave is exploring deployment on Sonic. The Aave community opened a governance discussion about deploying Aave V3 on Sonic, citing the network’s developer fee rebates as a compelling incentive.

Sonic Labs Ecosystem: Latest Platforms,.Core Infrastructure and Tools in the Son:
• Ethereum Bridge (Sonic Gateway & Rollup): Sonic’s trust-minimized Ethereum bridge, known as the Sonic Gateway, was upgraded into a Sonic Rollup integrated with Sonic’s validator set. This allows quick, low-fee asset transfers between Sonic and Ethereum.

• Chainlink Oracles & CCIP: By joining the Chainlink SCALE program, Sonic integrated Chainlink Data Feeds (price oracles) and CCIP for cross-chain messaging. This lets dApps access reliable price data and cross-chain functions.

• Rings Protocol (Yield-Backed Stablecoins): Rings deepens liquidity on Sonic by allowing users to deposit assets to mint yield-bearing tokens like scUSD or scETH, fully backed by collateral earning yield on Ethereum. Rings partnered with Lombard Finance to introduce scBTC, a yield-bearing Bitcoin asset on Sonic.

• Liquid Staking Services: Origin Protocol’s Origin Sonic (OS) token gives users a rebasing liquid staking option for S, while some protocols use stS (a non-rebasing staked S). Wrapped Sonic (wS) is also utilized by DEXes and NFT marketplaces.

• Developer Incentives (Fee Monetization): Sonic’s Fee Monetization (FeeM) model rewards dApp developers with up to 90% of gas fees generated by their contracts. This strong incentive (versus the standard 50% burn/50% validator fee split) encourages rapid dApp development.

Sonic Labs Ecosystem: Latest Platforms,.Most Active Tokens in the Sonic Network:
• S (Sonic’s Native Token): Core for fees, staking, and governance. Derived 1:1 from FTM, with ~3.175B supply at launch. A portion (~6%) is set aside for ecosystem airdrops.

• Wrapped Sonic (wS): The ERC-20 version of S for DeFi usage. PaintSwap and other apps rely on wS for transactions.

• Liquid Staking Tokens (OS and stS): OS (Origin Sonic) is a rebasing token for staked S, redeemable 1:1 while accruing rewards. stS serves a similar role in some protocols.

• ETH and BTC Derivatives (scETH, WETH, LBTC, scBTC): scETH and scBTC are yield-bearing derivatives minted by Rings. LBTC is Lombard’s liquid BTC. WETH/WBTC are bridged from Ethereum.

• Governance and LP Tokens: dApps like SpookySwap (BOO), Beethoven X (BEETS), and PaintSwap (BRUSH) have their own tokens for governance and yield. Core liquidity remains centered on major assets (S, USDC, ETH, BTC).
